# `silk/system/system_info`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The `SystemInfo` effect: facts about the computer and the running process that the operating
system reports, such as the host name, the memory, the processors, the network interfaces, the
current user, and the resource usage of the process.

## When to use
Require `&mut SystemInfo` in code that reports on the host or on its own process, such as an
`os` module of a language runtime, a status page, or a tool that sizes its work to the memory.
A test can provide fixed values. `silk.system.system_info_native` has the provider for native
programs.

## Details
Each operation asks the operating system again, so two calls can give different values. The
operations never wait for an event: each one makes a few system calls or reads a few files of
the system, and returns.

Text that the system reports, such as a host name, a path, or a user name, is returned as
owned `Bytes`, because the system does not promise UTF-8. Use `String.fromUtf8` when you need
text.

Environment variables are not read. A runtime that follows `HOME` or `TMPDIR` reads them with
`silk.system.host_input`, and uses [`UserInfo`](#UserInfo) when `HOME` is not set.

## Errors
- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) when the system cannot answer: the [`SystemInfoOperation`](#SystemInfoOperation) and the native
  error code.
- `OutOfMemoryError` when the `Allocator` cannot supply a returned value.

## Examples
### Read the memory of the computer
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.system.system_info { MemoryInfo, SystemInfo, SystemInfoError }
import silk.system.system_info_native { OsSystemInfo }

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut provider = OsSystemInfo.make()
  let result = run Effect.result(SystemInfo.memory()) |> Effect.provideMut<SystemInfo>(&mut provider)
  return match move result {
    Result<MemoryInfo, SystemInfoError>.Success { value } => {
      // The free memory is never more than the total.
      if value.total == 0 || value.free > value.total { 1 } else { 0 }
    }
    Result<MemoryInfo, SystemInfoError>.Failure { .. } => 1
  }
}
```

Import as `SystemInfo` with `import silk.system.system_info { SystemInfo }`.

<a id="SystemInfoError"></a>

## `SystemInfoError`

```silk
pub struct SystemInfoError
```

A failed [`SystemInfo`](#SystemInfo) operation: which one, and the native error code.

### Details
`code` is the `errno` value of the failed call, such as 2 (`ENOENT`) for a user id that has no
account, 3 (`ESRCH`) for a process that does not exist, or 13 (`EACCES`) for a priority that
the process may not set. For a failed Mach call on macOS, it is the `kern_return_t` value. It
is 0 when the system answered with data that is not valid.

<a id="SystemInfoError.operation"></a>

### Field `operation`

```silk
pub operation: SystemInfoOperation
```

The operation that failed.

<a id="SystemInfoError.code"></a>

### Field `code`

```silk
pub code: i32
```

The native error code, or 0 for data that is not valid.

<a id="MemoryInfo"></a>

## `MemoryInfo`

```silk
pub struct MemoryInfo
```

The memory of the computer, in bytes.

### Details
`free` is memory that nothing uses. `available` also counts memory that the system can take
back at once, such as file caches, so it is at least `free` on Linux (`MemAvailable`). On
macOS, `available` is the free page count, the same as `free`.

`limit` is the memory limit of the control group of the process, when it has one. A process
with a limit can use at most `limit.bytes - limit.used` more bytes, also when `available` is
larger.

<a id="MemoryInfo.total"></a>

### Field `total`

```silk

```

The physical memory, in bytes.

<a id="MemoryInfo.free"></a>

```silk

```

The memory that nothing uses, in bytes.

<a id="MemoryInfo.available"></a>

### Field `available`

```silk
pub available: u64
```

The memory that a new allocation can get without swapping, in bytes.

<a id="MemoryInfo.limit"></a>

### Field `limit`

```silk

```

The memory limit of the control group of the process, if there is one.

<a id="NetworkInterface"></a>

## `NetworkInterface`

```silk
pub struct NetworkInterface
```

One address of a network interface that is up.

### Details
An interface with more than one address gives one entry for each address, with the same name.
`mac` is the hardware address of the interface, or all zeros when it has none, such as a
loopback interface. `internal` is true for a loopback interface. `scopeId` is the scope of an
IPv6 address, such as the interface index of a link-local address, and 0 for IPv4.

<a id="ResourceUsage"></a>

## `ResourceUsage`

```silk
pub struct ResourceUsage
```

The resources that a process or a thread used, as `getrusage` reports them.

### Details
Times are in microseconds. `maxResidentBytes` is the largest resident memory so far, in bytes
on every system. The counters that a system does not keep are 0: Linux keeps no
`sharedMemory`, `unsharedData`, `unsharedStack`, `swaps`, `messagesSent`, `messagesReceived`,
or `signals`. For [`UsageScope.Thread`](#UsageScope.Thread) on macOS, only the two times are reported.

<a id="SystemInfo"></a>

## `SystemInfo`

```silk
pub service SystemInfo
```

The effect that reads facts about the computer and the running process from the operating
system.

### When to use

Require `&mut SystemInfo` in code that reports on the host or on its own process, such as an
`os` module of a language runtime. A test can provide fixed values. Use the provider in
`silk.system.system_info_native` in a native program.

### Details

Each operation asks the system again and returns without waiting for an event. Text that the
system reports is owned `Bytes`, because the system does not promise UTF-8. Environment
variables are not read: a runtime that follows `HOME` or `TMPDIR` reads them with
`silk.system.host_input`. Only [`SystemInfo.setPriority`](#SystemInfo.setPriority) changes the system.

<a id="SystemInfo.hostName"></a>

### Operation `hostName`

```silk
effect fn hostName() -> Bytes ! SystemInfoError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut SystemInfo | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the host name of the computer.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `HostName` if the system cannot report it.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="SystemInfo.kernel"></a>

### Operation `kernel`

```silk
effect fn kernel() -> KernelInfo ! SystemInfoError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut SystemInfo | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the names of the running kernel: name, release, version, and hardware.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `Kernel` if the system cannot report them.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.

<a id="SystemInfo.uptime"></a>

### Operation `uptime`

```silk
effect fn uptime() -> u64 ! SystemInfoError ? &mut SystemInfo
```

Returns the time since the computer started, in nanoseconds. It counts time asleep.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `Uptime` if the system cannot report it.

<a id="SystemInfo.loadAverage"></a>

### Operation `loadAverage`

```silk
effect fn loadAverage() -> [f64; 3] ! SystemInfoError ? &mut SystemInfo
```

Returns the 1, 5, and 15 minute load averages, in this order.

#### Details

A load average is the mean number of threads that ran or waited to run.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `LoadAverage` if the system cannot report them.

<a id="SystemInfo.memory"></a>

### Operation `memory`

```silk
effect fn memory() -> MemoryInfo ! SystemInfoError ? &mut SystemInfo
```

Returns the total, free, and available memory of the computer, and the memory limit of the
process when it has one.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `Memory` if the system cannot report them.

<a id="SystemInfo.processors"></a>

### Operation `processors`

```silk
effect fn processors() -> List<ProcessorInfo> ! SystemInfoError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut SystemInfo | &mut Allocator
```

Returns one entry for each logical processor that is online, in the order of the system.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `Processors` if the system cannot report them.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the list.

<a id="SystemInfo.availableParallelism"></a>

### Operation `availableParallelism`

```silk
effect fn availableParallelism() -> usize ! SystemInfoError ? &mut SystemInfo
```

Returns the number of processors that the process may run on, at least 1.

#### Details

On Linux, it counts the CPU affinity mask of the process, so it can be less than the number
of processors online. On macOS, it is the number of processors online.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `Parallelism` if the system cannot report it.

<a id="SystemInfo.networkInterfaces"></a>

### Operation `networkInterfaces`

```silk
effect fn networkInterfaces() -> List<NetworkInterface> ! SystemInfoError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut SystemInfo | &mut Allocator
```

Returns one entry for each address of each network interface that is up and running.

#### Details

Only IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are listed. An interface with no address is not listed.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `NetworkInterfaces` if the system cannot report them.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the list.


#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `User` if the account cannot be read, with code 2 (`ENOENT`) if the

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.

### Operation `user`

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.

<a id="SystemInfo.priority"></a>

### Operation `priority`

```silk
effect fn priority(pid: i32) -> i32 ! SystemInfoError ? &mut SystemInfo
```

Returns the scheduling priority of process `pid`, from -20 (first) to 19 (last). Process 0 is
the calling process.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `Priority`, with code 3 (`ESRCH`) if no process has the id.

<a id="SystemInfo.setPriority"></a>

### Operation `setPriority`

```silk
effect fn setPriority(pid: i32, value: i32) -> () ! SystemInfoError ? &mut SystemInfo
```

Sets the scheduling priority of process `pid` to `value`, from -20 (first) to 19 (last).
Process 0 is the calling process. The system limits a value outside the range to it.

#### Errors

- [`SystemInfoError`](#SystemInfoError) with `SetPriority`, with code 3 (`ESRCH`) if no process has the id, or
  13 (`EACCES`) or 1 (`EPERM`) if the process may not set that priority.
